prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying issue in `_handle_reconnection`: when SSE reconnection attempts are exhausted after a server disconnect, the client previously just returned silently, leaving the caller's in-flight request waiting forever with no response. #2395 makes the exhausted-retry branch construct a JSONRPCError and send it directly to the affected request's `read_stream_writer` (guarded by `isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications aren't given a spurious response). #3098 instead has that code path raise a `StreamableHTTPError`, adding a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull that error back out of the anyio `ExceptionGroup` it gets wrapped in. These are two different fixes for the same trigger (reconnection-attempts-exhausted) and the same symptom (caller hangs indefinitely). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying issue in `_handle_reconnection`: when SSE reconnection attempts are exhausted after a server disconnect, the client previously just returned silently, leaving the caller's in-flight request waiting forever with no response. #2395 makes the exhausted-retry branch construct a JSONRPCError and send it directly to the affected request's `read_stream_writer` (guarded by `isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications aren't given a spurious response). #3098 instead has that code path raise a `StreamableHTTPError`, adding a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull that error back out of the anyio `ExceptionGroup` it gets wrapped in. These are two different fixes for the same trigger (reconnection-attempts-exhausted) and the same symptom (caller hangs indefinitely). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395's fix is scoped to the single failing request: it sends a JSONRPCError only via that request's own `read_stream_writer`, so other concurrently in-flight requests on separate streams are unaffected, and it explicitly guards with `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which have no id) aren't erroneously answered. #3098's approach raises `StreamableHTTPError` through the anyio task group, which propagates as a group-level failure and would tear down the whole session/task group rather than just failing the one affected request - a larger blast radius for the same failure. #3098's diff also includes an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`) unconnected to the reconnection fix, adding unrelated surface area to review.

prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both address the same root cause: the write-side memory object stream in stdio_server is created with buffer size 0, causing a handler's send of its final response to block/deadlock while the stdout_writer task is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 generalizes this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as new keyword parameters, both still defaulting to 0, so the blocking bug persists unless a caller explicitly opts in. #2654 instead fixes the default behavior directly by hardcoding the write stream's buffer to 1, resolving the deadlock out of the box, and adds a targeted regression test (BlockingStdout) reproducing the exact scenario of a queued response blocked behind an in-flight progress notification. (2 PRs)

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a restart (or any cold start where `OAuthContext.oauth_metadata` is unset in-memory), `_refresh_token()` has no authorization-server metadata to find the token endpoint, so refreshing a still-valid refresh_token fails or falls back to full re-authorization instead of silently refreshing. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3263 solves this without changing the `TokenStorage` protocol: it re-runs AS metadata discovery on-demand before a cold-start refresh, adds an issuer-binding check on the (re)discovered metadata, and tracks `eager_discovery_attempted` so a metadata-less server isn't re-probed on every refresh. #2492 instead adds new `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods to the `TokenStorage` protocol (a breaking/additive API change every storage implementation must adopt to get the fix) and has no equivalent issuer-binding validation, so a stale or mismatched persisted metadata blob could be trusted without verification.

members.author: yaowubarbara

clusters.pick_reason: #2395's fix is scoped to the single failing request: it sends a JSONRPCError only via that request's own `read_stream_writer`, so other concurrently in-flight requests on separate streams are unaffected, and it explicitly guards with `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which have no id) aren't erroneously answered. #3098's approach raises `StreamableHTTPError` through the anyio task group, which propagates as a group-level failure and would tear down the whole session/task group rather than just failing the one affected request - a larger blast radius for the same failure. #3098's diff also includes an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`) unconnected to the reconnection fix, adding unrelated surface area to review.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying issue in `_handle_reconnection`: when SSE reconnection attempts are exhausted after a server disconnect, the client previously just returned silently, leaving the caller's in-flight request waiting forever with no response. #2395 makes the exhausted-retry branch construct a JSONRPCError and send it directly to the affected request's `read_stream_writer` (guarded by `isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications aren't given a spurious response). #3098 instead has that code path raise a `StreamableHTTPError`, adding a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull that error back out of the anyio `ExceptionGroup` it gets wrapped in. These are two different fixes for the same trigger (reconnection-attempts-exhausted) and the same symptom (caller hangs indefinitely). (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #3263 solves this without changing the `TokenStorage` protocol: it re-runs AS metadata discovery on-demand before a cold-start refresh, adds an issuer-binding check on the (re)discovered metadata, and tracks `eager_discovery_attempted` so a metadata-less server isn't re-probed on every refresh. #2492 instead adds new `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods to the `TokenStorage` protocol (a breaking/additive API change every storage implementation must adopt to get the fix) and has no equivalent issuer-binding validation, so a stale or mismatched persisted metadata blob could be trusted without verification.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both address the same root cause: the write-side memory object stream in stdio_server is created with buffer size 0, causing a handler's send of its final response to block/deadlock while the stdout_writer task is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 generalizes this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as new keyword parameters, both still defaulting to 0, so the blocking bug persists unless a caller explicitly opts in. #2654 instead fixes the default behavior directly by hardcoding the write stream's buffer to 1, resolving the deadlock out of the box, and adds a targeted regression test (BlockingStdout) reproducing the exact scenario of a queued response blocked behind an in-flight progress notification.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395's fix is scoped to the single failing request: it sends a JSONRPCError only via that request's own `read_stream_writer`, so other concurrently in-flight requests on separate streams are unaffected, and it explicitly guards with `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications (which have no id) aren't erroneously answered. #3098's approach raises `StreamableHTTPError` through the anyio task group, which propagates as a group-level failure and would tear down the whole session/task group rather than just failing the one affected request - a larger blast radius for the same failure. #3098's diff also includes an unrelated change (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`) unconnected to the reconnection fix, adding unrelated surface area to review.

members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same underlying issue in `_handle_reconnection`: when SSE reconnection attempts are exhausted after a server disconnect, the client previously just returned silently, leaving the caller's in-flight request waiting forever with no response. #2395 makes the exhausted-retry branch construct a JSONRPCError and send it directly to the affected request's `read_stream_writer` (guarded by `isinstance(..., JSONRPCRequest)` so notifications aren't given a spurious response). #3098 instead has that code path raise a `StreamableHTTPError`, adding a new `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull that error back out of the anyio `ExceptionGroup` it gets wrapped in. These are two different fixes for the same trigger (reconnection-attempts-exhausted) and the same symptom (caller hangs indefinitely). (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: #3263 solves this without changing the `TokenStorage` protocol: it re-runs AS metadata discovery on-demand before a cold-start refresh, adds an issuer-binding check on the (re)discovered metadata, and tracks `eager_discovery_attempted` so a metadata-less server isn't re-probed on every refresh. #2492 instead adds new `get_oauth_metadata`/`set_oauth_metadata` methods to the `TokenStorage` protocol (a breaking/additive API change every storage implementation must adopt to get the fix) and has no equivalent issuer-binding validation, so a stale or mismatched persisted metadata blob could be trusted without verification.
